name: Nicholas C. Park
tagline: Software Engineer · AI Agents · Applied Cognition
description: Software engineer, AI researcher, and founder. Reinforcement learning, multi-agent systems, and applied cognition.
about: I build machine learning systems and study how they improve through experience. My background spans quantitative modeling, software engineering, and graduate study at Georgia Tech. I care about the full experimental loop: establishing a baseline, measuring behavior, and using the results to improve the system.

My graduate course projects explored cooperation in multi-agent reinforcement learning and how training-data selection affects language-model performance. I’m interested in agents that learn from feedback and adapt as conditions change, especially in visual and interactive environments.

interests.name: AI Agents & Multi-Agent Systems
interests.description: Building and reasoning about autonomous agents — from single-agent RL to multi-agent coordination. Practical agent engineering (LangGraph, tool-use architectures) alongside theoretical foundations.

interests.name: Reinforcement Learning
interests.description: Deep RL methods applied to complex environments. MADDPG in multi-agent settings, DDQN for control problems, SARSA for tabular methods. Interest spans from practical implementation to theoretical guarantees.

interests.name: Human Cognition & Metacognition
interests.description: How humans think about thinking. The via-negativa project explores negative perception as a metacognitive skill — applying subtraction to thought itself. Where AI meets cognitive science.

interests.name: Category Theory & Mathematical Foundations
interests.description: Abstract mathematical structures as a lens for understanding computation, learning, and cognition. Compositional thinking applied beyond pure mathematics.

interests.name: Natural Language Processing
interests.description: Transformer architectures, sequence-to-sequence models, adversarial robustness in NLI. A foundation that informs current agent work.
